deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1983–84 study of systems of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. It sets up the combinatorics of an arrangement as a 'map' (carte) on RP^2 and describes it with the cartographic-group formalism that also appears in Esquisse d'un programme.

(1) Generators and relations. Top left: ρ_s = σ2σ1 and ρ_f = σ1σ0, so σ1 = ρ_f^{σ0} (the conjugate of ρ_f by σ0). Also ρ_sρ_f = σ2σ1σ1σ0 = σ2σ0 =: σ. In the language of the Esquisse:
- σ0, σ1, σ2 are the three flag involutions.
- ρ_s is rotation about a vertex (sommet).
- ρ_f is rotation about a face.
- σ = σ2σ0 is the edge involution ρ_a.
The identity ρ_sρ_f = σ is the relation ρ_sρ_aρ_f = 1 rewritten using σ^2 = 1. This relies on (σ0σ2)^2 = 1, which the page does not state but which the reading requires.

(2) Encoding a flag. A flag (vertex s, edge, face) of the map cut out by the arrangement is encoded locally. Take a crossing s of two orange pseudo-lines, with T the small triangular cell adjacent to s (hatched). Then draw a transversal pseudo-line D0 (dashed green) through s, flanked by parallel copies D and D'. D cuts off the triangle T, so D0 is 'pushed' across s. The flag is the triple (D0, β*, ω*):
- β* is a transverse orientation of D0, i.e. the direction in which it is pushed.
- α* is the corresponding orientation along D0.
- ω* = −α*∧β* is a local orientation of the plane.

(3) Dual picture (sketch labelled Δ_s). The vertex s becomes a line Δ_s in the dual plane, and the lines D, D' through s become points σ_D, σ_D' on Δ_s, with vectors α (along Δ_s), β and ω = α∧β. The next page develops this duality between X and X̌ for a 'triangle' T and its dual T', and compares the induced orientations.

(4) The action. The central diagram gives the action on (D0, β*, ω*):
- σ0 ↦ (D0, β*, −ω*). Its dual description: σ0 reverses α and keeps σ_D, σ_D', β.
- σ2 ↦ (D0, −β*, −ω*). Its dual description: σ2 swaps σ_D and σ_D', reverses β, keeps α.
- σ = σ2σ0 ↦ (D0, −β*, ω*).
- σ1 moves the transversal along the edge to the neighbouring crossing on the same line. The result is shown as two alternatives (the triangle T near the old or the new vertex), each with orientation −ω*.
- ρ_s and ρ_f are drawn as the corresponding composite moves. The ρ_f picture shows the triangle T carried to an adjacent triangle T1, with the instruction 'prenons bien des triangles'.

Purpose: to give a concrete, self-dual description of the flag set of a pseudo-line arrangement as a C2-set (a set acted on by the cartographic group). This prepares the projective-duality analysis of the next page.
errors: The relation ρ_sρ_f = σ holds only if σ means σ2σ0, and the identification with the edge involution needs (σ0σ2)^2 = 1. This is implicit; the page does not state it.

The σ1 move is drawn as an ambiguous pair ('ou') of pictures. The page does not settle which triangle convention is canonical ('prenons bien des triangles' suggests the choice is still being fixed). This is a gap, not an error.
Signs: ω* = −α*∧β* versus ω = α∧β is a deliberate convention change between the primal and dual pictures. Its consistency with the dual-side descriptions of σ0 and σ2 is not verified on the page.

ideas.what: Cartographic group generated by flag involutions σ0, σ1, σ2, with rotations ρ_s = σ2σ1, ρ_f = σ1σ0 and edge involution σ2σ0
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group C2 / flag (monodromy) group of a map; maps as C2-sets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on cartographic groups and dessins

ideas.what: Viewing a pseudo-line arrangement in RP^2 as a map on the non-orientable surface RP^2 and encoding its flags
ideas.modern_name: cell complex / map of a pseudoline arrangement; flags of oriented-matroid face lattice

ideas.what: Encoding a flag by a transversal pseudo-line D0 through a vertex, with a transverse orientation and a local orientation, and a dual description via the pencil line Δ_s in the dual plane
ideas.modern_name: local flag coordinates; projective duality of pseudoline arrangements (dual arrangement / allowable sequences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, duality of pseudoline arrangements, 1980s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck applies his cartographic-group formalism (σ0, σ1, σ2 and the 'dessins' framework of the Esquisse) directly to pseudo-line arrangements. He describes the flag involutions through a self-dual (point/line) encoding, so that projective duality of the arrangement should act on the C2-set of flags. This link between the map-theoretic C2-set of an arrangement and its pseudo-line duality is not standard in the arrangements or oriented-matroid literature.
missed.quote: ρ_s = σ2σ1 ... ρ_f = σ1σ0 ... ρ_sρ_f = σ ... σ0 change α en −α, en gardant σ_D, σ_D', β ; σ2 échange σ_D et σ_D', change β en −β, garde α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a dessin-theoretic (Belyi-type, Galois-action) viewpoint on pseudoline arrangements. It could also give an explicit description of how duality acts on flag groups, which is relevant to the combinatorial classification of arrangements. The idea is modest, and the page only sets up notation.

deep.surprise_reason: The cartographic-group formalism is published in the Esquisse, and the map structure of pseudoline arrangements is classical. What is new here is only the specific use of σ0, σ1, σ2 with a dual (point/line) encoding of flags in the pseudo-line setting, presented as unfinished notational set-up.
transcription_corrections: Top left: the third line reads 'ρ_sρ_f = σ'. The second line's 'σ1 = ρ_f^{σ0}' denotes conjugation of ρ_f by σ0.
'α*, β*, ω* non orientés': the underlined word is hard to read ('non' or 'aussi'). Given the explicit sign in ω* = −α*∧β*, it may not be 'non'.
The arrows from (D0, β*, ω*) are labelled σ0 → (D0, β*, −ω*), σ1 → (pair of pictures), σ2 → (D0, −β*, −ω*), and σ ↦ (D0, −β*, ω*). ρ_s and ρ_f label curved arrows to the top pictures.
The printed typescript in the background (DATASETS PICTURES, DESTINATION, CLASS, COPIES ...) is computer-paper header text, not mathematics.
